from_quote: The imposition of duties on imported articles
rationale: Names "the imposition of duties on imported articles" as one of the things the States are "by the plan of the convention" prohibited from doing, the prohibition in this clause.
to_quote: lay any Imposts or Duties on Imports

rationale: Names "the emission of paper money" as one of the things the States are "by the plan of the convention" prohibited from doing; this clause is where the plan bars the States from emitting bills of credit.

from_quote: They are not, for instance, to emit paper money; but the interdiction results from the Constitution
rationale: Names, as one of "the restrictions upon the authority of the State legislatures," that they are "not ... to emit paper money," an interdiction it says "results from the Constitution"; this clause is where the plan bars the States from emitting bills of credit.

from_quote: It has also been asked, what need of the word “equity
rationale: Takes up the word "equity" in the clause under review, putting the word in quotation marks.

from_quote: the national legislature will have ample authority to make such EXCEPTIONS, and to prescribe such regulations
rationale: Echoes this clause's words "such Exceptions" and "such Regulations" as the Congress shall make, putting "EXCEPTIONS" in capitals.
to_quote: with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make
